root.name: Petrov's Defense: Paulsen Attack
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Nxe5 d6 4. Nc4

overview: In 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 White retreats with 4.Nc4 instead of 4.Nf3. After 4...Nxe4 White usually plays 5.Nc3 Nxc3 6.dxc3 (or 5.Qe2), reaching a quiet symmetrical-ish position with the e-file open. Black develops with ...Be7, ...Nc6 and ...O-O and equalises easily; White has a tiny space edge and no real attack.

white_ideas.idea: Trade knights on c3 and recapture with the d-pawn for quick development
Play Be3, Qd2 and castle long or short
Use the open e-file and the Nc4-e3 manoeuvre

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and trade pieces to reach equality

typical_structures.structure: Symmetrical-ish structure with White doubled c-pawns after dxc3 and an open e-file

character.notes: Quiet, heavily traded, hard for either side to win quickly.

structure.notes: Symmetrical exchange structure with an open e-file.

approach.notes: Standard line of a main defence.

level.notes: Plans are simple; Black needs to know the equalising set-ups.

character.reason: Black's Petrov set-up is hard to break down and play is steady.
